html:
The Temple of Poseidon is a Doric marble temple on Cape Sounion, the southern tip of Attica, built around 444 to 440 BCE. Its white columns stand on a cliff high above the sea.

The cape had been holy ground for centuries. An older temple to Poseidon on the same spot was destroyed by the Persians during the invasion of Xerxes in 480 BCE, and Athens rebuilt it in the years of Pericles. Some scholars think the same architect designed the Temple of Hephaestus in Athens.

The temple mattered for a sea power. Ships sailing to Piraeus rounded the cape, and the temple was the first sight of home for Athenian sailors. The silver mines of Laurion, which paid for the Athenian fleet, lay just to the north.

Several columns still stand. The poet Lord Byron carved his name on one of them in the early 19th century.
sum: The Temple of Poseidon is a Doric marble temple on Cape Sounion, the southern tip of Attica, built around 444 to 440 BCE. Its white columns stand on a cliff high above the sea.
